mission_09: Quantum optimization algorithms like QAOA and VQE use parameterized quantum circuits to find optimal solutions to combinatorial and eigenvalue problems. QAOA (Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm) alternates between applying a cost Hamiltonian (encoding the objective function) and a mixer Hamiltonian (exploring the solution space), with parameters gamma and beta optimized classically. VQE (Variational Quantum Eigensolver) uses a hardware-efficient ansatz (alternating single-qubit rotations and entangling gates) to prepare trial states, minimizing the energy expectation value to find ground states. Both algorithms use classical optimization with numerical gradients to update quantum circuit parameters. In this mission, you implement QAOA with cost and mixer unitaries via Hamiltonian exponentiation, VQE with a hardware-efficient ansatz, numerical gradient computation, and classical optimization loops.
